sources.title: Human History Map 1500 BCE borders
sources.note: First exact two-part target geometry, holes, bounds and decoded point owners.

sources.title: Human History Map 1000 BCE borders

sources.title: Human History Map 700 BCE borders
sources.note: Third interval and exact coordinate identity with the 1000 BCE geometry.

sources.title: Human History Map 500 BCE borders
sources.note: Two simultaneous exact-id Polygon features, Adena cutout and revised southern edge.

sources.title: Human History Map 400 BCE borders
sources.note: The two features recombine as one MultiPolygon with a coordinate revision.

sources.title: Human History Map 323 BCE borders
sources.note: One-position revision to the small Long Island component and changed coordinate hash.

sources.title: Human History Map 300 BCE borders
sources.note: The 323 BCE geometry is copied exactly into the next observed interval.

sources.title: Human History Map 200 BCE borders

sources.title: Human History Map 100 BCE borders
sources.note: Endpoint redraw into several named archaeological labels and extensive blank space.

sources.title: Smith and Yarnell, Initial Formation of an Indigenous Crop Complex in Eastern North America
sources.note: Direct Riverton plant remains, AMS chronology, clay floors, pits, hearths and flotation evidence.

sources.title: Bruce D. Smith, Origins of Agriculture in Eastern North America
sources.note: Smithsonian synthesis of independent plant domestication, seed measurement, storage and evidence limits.

sources.title: Pompeani and colleagues, Refining the Chronology of North American Copper-Using Traditions
sources.note: Bayesian radiocarbon model, Great Lakes copper chronology, aquatic foods and regional variation.

sources.title: Hill and colleagues, Early Metal Use and Crematory Practices in the American Southeast
sources.note: Dated St. Catherines Island cremation, Great Lakes copper sourcing, shell ring context and inference.

sources.title: Michael Russo, Archaic Shell Rings of the Southeast United States
sources.note: National Park Service archaeological synthesis of shell rings, chronology, settlement and preservation.

sources.title: Andrus and Thompson, Mollusk Collection at the Sapelo Island Shell Ring Complex
sources.note: Shell chemistry and growth increments used to test habitats and collection seasons.

sources.title: Victor Thompson, Questioning Complexity at Sapelo Island
sources.note: University dissertation on shell-ring households, gatherings, labor, social organization and uncertainty.

sources.title: Bronwyn Matlick, Vessel Technology at the Sapelo Shell Ring Complex
sources.note: University research on fiber-tempered vessel manufacture, technological change and sampled ceramic evidence.

sources.title: UNESCO, Monumental Earthworks of Poverty Point
sources.note: Chronology, designed earthworks, floodplain setting, exchange and hunter-fisher-gatherer achievement.

sources.title: National Park Service, Monumental Earthworks of Poverty Point
sources.note: Residential and ceremonial landscape, foods, imported stone, cooking objects and research uncertainty.

sources.title: National Park Service, Archaic Culture at Ocmulgee
sources.note: Regional base camps, storage pits, house floors, horticultural experiments and early pottery.

sources.title: National Park Service, Initial Woodland
sources.note: Regional pottery chronology, coil construction, net sinkers and exchange around Lake Superior.

sources.title: National Park Service, Ohio's Prehistoric Past
sources.note: Archaeological period labels, Ohio Woodland developments, mounds, pottery and native crops.

sources.title: Bradley Lepper, How Old Is the Adena Mound?
sources.note: Ohio History Connection account of dating evidence, uncertainty and an archaeological type-site name.

sources.title: Bradley Lepper, The Adena Pipe: Icon of Ancient Ohio
sources.note: Object history, skilled stone carving, archaeological context and limits on identifying the depicted person.

sources.title: West Virginia Department of Arts, Culture and History, Grave Creek Mound
sources.note: Institutional site history for a regional mound, construction sequence and early destructive excavation.

sources.title: Kentucky Heritage Council, Indian Knoll
sources.note: Official site synthesis of shell midden excavation, tools, people and dogs in burials.

sources.title: Kentucky Archaeological Survey, Green River Archaic Hunters and Gatherers
sources.note: Public archaeological synthesis of subsistence, households, burial, dental health, injury and interpretation.

sources.title: Kentucky Heritage Council, Archaeology of the Woodland Period
sources.note: Regional synthesis of textiles, caves, native crops, settlement and Early Woodland chronology.

sources.title: National Park Service, Native Americans at Mammoth Cave
sources.note: Direct cave evidence for torches, sandals, gourd bowls, images, minerals and uncertainty over use.

sources.title: National Park Service, Cave Discoveries from the Past
sources.note: Cave artifacts, past mistreatment of human remains, NAGPRA-era respect and tribal consultation.

sources.title: National Park Service, Wildland Fire at Mammoth Cave
sources.note: Pollen evidence for controlled burning, forest openings, food plants and torch materials.

sources.title: National Park Service Southeast Archeological Center, Learn about Archeology
sources.note: Institutional explanation of archaeological features, trash, gardens, houses, burials and methods.

sources.title: Maryland Archaeological Conservation Laboratory, Woodcock Farm Shell Middens
sources.note: Professional survey and testing of dated coastal shell middens and archaeological sampling limits.

sources.title: Munoz and colleagues, Environmental and Cultural Change in the Northeastern United States
sources.note: Regional archaeological and paleoenvironmental chronology, population proxies, climate and causal uncertainty.

sources.title: Ontario Archaeological Society, Summary of Ontario Archaeology
sources.note: Regional chronology, early fish weir, copper, burial variation and Great Lakes evidence.

sources.title: Yale Human Relations Area Files, Eastern Late Archaic Summary
sources.note: Scholarly regional synthesis emphasizing environmental, technological, subsistence and mortuary diversity.

sources.title: Lindsay Gilliland, Late Archaic Children's Burials in the Pickwick Basin
sources.note: University research on childhood, burial goods, skeletal pathology, sample limits and ethical interpretation.

sources.title: Karl Reinhard, Archaeoparasitology in North America
sources.note: Peer-reviewed review of coprolites, skeletons, latrine soils, parasite evidence and identification limits.

sources.title: National Park Service, Hopewell Farming
sources.note: Later regional comparison for Eastern Agricultural Complex crops, gathering and small fields.

sources.title: UNESCO, Hopewell Ceremonial Earthworks
sources.note: World Heritage evidence for later Ohio earthworks, precise geometry, exchange and Indigenous achievement.

sources.title: National Park Service, Eastern Woodland Habitat
sources.note: Later Ohio evidence for foods, forest management, bark houses, hunting and native crops.

sources.title: Smithsonian Libraries, Foraging and Farming in the Eastern Woodlands
sources.note: Scholarly volume record stressing native crops, foodway variability and changing interpretations.

sources.title: National Park Service, Identifying Cultural Affiliation under NAGPRA
sources.note: Consultation requirements and recognition that an earlier group may relate to multiple living nations.

sources.title: National Museum of the American Indian, Woodlands
sources.note: Museum synthesis of deep regional history, exchange, objects and living Native cultural continuity.

scopeNotes: New text needs independent review; earlier hashes do not certify it.
Map endpoints are not historical founding or extinction dates.
Agent researched a disjoint batch; integration and structural checks are not independent historical certification.
Imported border coordinates remain unchanged. Historical events and map coverage are distinguished in prose; see batchIdentityNotes for conflicts.

proposedOverrides.summary: Eastern North American atlas umbrella, 1500 to 100 BCE.

batchIdentityNotes: The exact indexed id is preserved solely as a historical-basemap display key for circa 1500 to 100 BCE.
The label is an editorial umbrella, not one people, language, state, economy or archaeological culture.
Eight exact observed intervals continuously cover the indexed lifetime.
The polygon spans Atlantic Canada to Florida and the upper Mississippi while leaving conspicuous places blank.
At 500 BCE the target is stored as two exact-id features and the Ohio Valley is cut into an Adena label.
The 100 BCE endpoint is a redraw into regional archaeological labels and blank space rather than a shared fall.
Direct finds, scientific inference and later localized comparisons remain explicitly distinguished.
No contemporaneous written-language sample is supplied because no deciphered script is securely attributable to the umbrella.
Predecessor and successor arrays remain empty because the atlas category is not a historical polity or people.
